text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Communications Ministry allocates 10 million dinars ($33 million) to launch a second mobile telecommunications firm.
- Kuwait Finance House KFHS.KW completes a $10 million commercial complex in Bangladesh.
- Security sources say stateless Arab issue to be resolved in 1997. Some 100,000 people who reside in Kuwait without nationality documents are demanding Kuwaiti citizenship.

- Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah visited Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah in Rome on Tuesday. Sheikh Saad flew to Britain and to the United States for medical checks after an emergency colon surgery in Kuwait in early March.

- Government official says that major technical, economic, political and financial challenges are hampering the plan to replace foreign employees by Kuwaitis. Kuwait, with a population of 1.25 million expatriates and 710,000 Kuwaitis, has a target of replacing foreigners at an annual rate of 10 percent.
- Some 250 petroleum engineers graduate from Kuwait University.
- Twelve percent of Kuwaitis over 20 years of age are diabetic.
